title: Ex-MP Hadházy Publishes NVVH Leadership Applicant Records, Calls for Anti-Corruption Chief Unger's Resignation
detail: Former independent MP Ákos Hadházy published excerpts on September 10 from what he described as the full database of applicants for leadership posts at the new anti-corruption body NVVH, arguing that agency president Anna Unger would not have ranked among the top 60 of 96 applicants on professional merit. Hadházy said the selection process was 'absolute theater' and called on Unger to resign, though he stopped short of publishing the full list, saying redacted entries would still be identifiable given applicants' qualifications and workplaces; he shared only the name of Dávid Jancsics, who had withdrawn before the interview stage. The parliamentary Justice and Constitutional Affairs Committee had advanced three finalists to interviews based on top scores, but contradictions have emerged over whether a formal scoring system was actually used. The NVVH, established to investigate Orbán-era state asset misappropriation, began operations September 1 under Unger's six-year term.

media.caption: Ákos Hadházy alleges the NVVH leadership selection process favored Anna Unger
